description: Hard exclusion rules for remy-secure false-positive filtering. Findings matching any enabled rule are automatically discarded.

rules.description: Denial of Service vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion attacks.
Secrets or credentials stored on disk if otherwise secured by file permissions or encryption.
Rate limiting concerns or service overload scenarios.
Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.
Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields without proven security impact.
Input sanitization concerns for GitHub Action workflows unless clearly triggerable via untrusted input.
Lack of hardening measures without a concrete vulnerability. Code is not expected to implement all security best practices.
Race conditions or timing attacks that are theoretical rather than practically exploitable.
Vulnerabilities related to outdated third-party libraries. Managed separately.
Memory safety issues (buffer overflows, use-after-free) in memory-safe languages (Rust, Go, Java, Python, JS/TS).
Files that are only unit tests or only used as part of running tests.
Log spoofing concerns. Outputting unsanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability by itself.
SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF requires control of host or protocol.
Including user-controlled content in AI system prompts is not a vulnerability in this context.
Injecting untrusted content into a regex or regex DoS concerns.
Insecure documentation. Findings in markdown or documentation files are not vulnerabilities.
Lack of audit logs is not a vulnerability.
